learning: If line_loss_events falls to 0 and max_error drops below 0.06 m, the speed and gain were the limit. If progress falls with no line loss change, the lower speed is too slow. If the loss persists at 1 per run with max_error at the floor, the controller is not the limit either.
notes: Controller-only change on the iteration 5 geometry: base_speed 1.6 to 1.0, kp 1.4 to 2.5, kd 0.15 to 0.4. Geometry is the Builder's proposal unchanged.
rationale: Iterations 0 to 8 (540 trials, all off_track) show max_error pinned at the 0.06 m floor, one line loss per run from iteration 3 on, and low steering_oscillation (0.07 to 0.16). The robot drifts off the line rather than oscillating, and no geometry lever has moved it. I therefore adopt the Builder's proposal exactly, the iteration 5 geometry (best score 53.6775, 0.016 m footprint, 20 mm pitch at y = 0.04 m, track 0.10 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, mass 0.4 kg), and change only the controller. Iterations 1 and 2 showed that kp 1.2 to 1.4 and kd 0.1 to 0.15 move nothing, so a small gain change alone will not help. Progress of 0.11 to 0.16 with off_track endings suggests the robot is carrying too much speed into the bends for its turn authority. I therefore lower base_speed from 1.6 to 1.0 to shorten the lateral error per unit distance, raise kp from 1.4 to 2.5 for more correction per unit error, and raise kd from 0.15 to 0.4 to damp the larger gain. ki stays at 0.05 and the weights and last_direction recovery are unchanged. Risk: the lower speed may stall the run (the 0.002 per 50 steps rule) or push the finish past 3 s. I expect the line loss and max_error to move, but I make no claim on the result.
